item: Basis: civil code article 138 - whoever has the use, management and control of a thing is its custodian and answers for the harm it causes; check the paragraph that sets the presumption and the paragraph that frees the custodian (external cause: act of the victim, of a third party, unforeseeable event, force majeure).

Custody: establish that the defendant had use, management and control (usage, direction, controle) of the thing at the time of the harm; owner is presumed custodian but custody may have passed (theft, lease, loan, employee use).
Element: the harm itself (material or moral) and its date; the thing's active role (positive intervention) in producing it.
Element: causal link between the thing and the harm; the defendant may rebut only by proving an external cause that he could not foresee.
Burden of proof: the victim proves custody, the harm and the thing's intervention; fault need not be proved; the custodian bears the proof of the external cause.
Animals: civil code article 139 - the keeper of an animal (owner or user) answers for the harm it causes even if it strayed or escaped, unless he proves an external cause; check its exact paragraphs.

Buildings: civil code article 140 - the owner of a building answers for its collapse, total or partial, unless he proves it is not due to lack of maintenance, age or a construction defect; check also the paragraph on the neighbour threatened by a building who may ask for preventive measures.

Fire: civil code article 140 bis (or the fire paragraph of article 140) - whoever holds a property in which a fire starts answers to third parties only if fault is proved; this is a boundary, not strict liability.
Boundary: harm by a person's own act - civil code article 124 (fault-based tort), not custody of a thing.
Boundary: liability for others (minors, employees) - civil code articles 134 to 137; employee driving the employer's vehicle.

Boundary: road traffic accidents - ordinance 74-15 on compulsory motor insurance and the compensation regime for road accident victims; a car accident is not claimed under article 138 against the insurer.
Boundary: defective products - civil code article 140 bis (producer liability) since law 05-10.

Boundary: contractual relation between the parties (tenant against landlord for water leak, lessee duty under lease articles; contractor and architect ten-year liability, civil code article 554) - contractual liability excludes the tort regime.
Boundary: work accidents - social security law 83-13, not civil custody liability against the employer.

Boundary: damage caused by a public body's thing or vehicle - administrative jurisdiction (code of civil and administrative procedure articles 800 and 801), except vehicle damage of article 802 which stays with the ordinary courts.

Compensation: civil code articles 131 and 182 - the judge assesses the harm under articles 182 and 182 bis (actual loss and lost gain, moral damage); check whether 131 allows reserving the right to revise the assessment.
Compensation: civil code article 132 - form of compensation (money, instalments, rent, restoration in kind).
Contributory fault of the victim: civil code article 177 - the judge may reduce or refuse compensation where the victim contributed to the harm.

Limitation: civil code article 133 - the tort damages claim is time-barred after fifteen years from the day of the harmful act; check whether there is a shorter period and whether the court raises it of its own motion (civil code article 321: not raised by the court).
Limitation counting: civil code articles 314 onward on counting by days, suspension and interruption (claim filed, acknowledgement).

Criminal case on the same facts: if the harm results from an offence (e.g. dog attack, injury), the civil action may follow the criminal one; criminal-holds-civil rule; limitation of the civil action not before the public action (code of criminal procedure article 10).
Formal notice: no formal notice needed for tort compensation (civil code article 181); check the formal-notice module.
Court: the civil section of the tribunal (code of civil and administrative procedure article 32 and the court-sections module).
Territory: in tort matters, the court of the place where the harmful act occurred (code of civil and administrative procedure article 39), otherwise the defendant's domicile (article 37).
Exits: administrative courts when the custodian is a public administrative body; criminal judge when the plaintiff joins as civil party; commercial court only if a commercial dispute.
Prior steps: none required by law; an expert finding (constat by a bailiff) is evidence, not a condition of admissibility.

Documents: bailiff's report of findings (constat), photographs, expert report if any, proof of ownership or custody of the thing (title, lease, vehicle card), medical certificates for bodily injury, invoices or estimates of repair.
Requests: damages with an amount; repair in kind; in the alternative appointment of an expert to assess the harm (code of civil and administrative procedure articles 125 onward).
Accessory requests: costs, provisional execution, interest only from the judgment; check the accessory-requests module.
Petition formalities: code of civil and administrative procedure article 15 and the petition-formal-elements module (identities, facts, grounds, documents, fees, Arabic).
Standing: the victim himself or his heirs; insurer subrogated after paying the victim.
Amendments: law 05-10 of 20 June 2005 amended articles 124 onward and added 140 bis and 182 bis; check the version in force of articles 131, 138, 140.
